title: Clean ocean — no spill

gallery.blurb: Open ocean, nothing on it. Does the system say so?

notes: Zenodo Part III clean-ocean scene (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13761290, CC-BY - the attribution is mandatory and must appear on a slide). LOCATION IS REAL: the tile carries EPSG:4326 and a real geotransform, so bounds.json holds its true box (W 35.1126 S 34.6950 E 35.2966 N 34.8790), open water in the eastern Mediterranean. No place name is asserted beyond that, because the box is measured and a place name would be inferred. TIME IS NOT KNOWN: the TIFF carries no acquisition timestamp (the only tag is AREA_OR_POINT), so detection_time is a deliberate 1970 epoch sentinel - there is no real value to recover and none is implied. Say both halves out loud: we show you where, we do not know when, we do not guess. provenance is 'benchmark', so the CNN scene classifier scored this scene and its confidence is a model probability, not a rule margin (Master 6.3). Expected Stage 1 output: a FeatureCollection with zero features classified 'oil' AND zero radar contacts - that is the correct result, not a failure. WHY THIS SCENE REPLACED P3_No oil_00091 (Soum, 13 Sept): 00091 was nominated on statistics alone - it was the 'hardest' no-oil scene by dark-feature depth - and the plot was never looked at. It is not ocean. It is farmland in the Ghab plain: field parcels, roads, a settlement and the Orontes river, at 35.14-35.32 N, roughly 150 km inland from the Gulf of Iskenderun this file previously named. Its 31 'radar contacts' were buildings and vehicles, and the blurb asking whether the system can tell traffic from a spill would have presented land clutter as marine traffic to a judge who could check it on any map. 00027 is genuinely open water: median -26.9 dB, MAD 0.47, full 1st-99th percentile spread 3.6 dB, zero pixels above -5 dB, and the ship detector returns ZERO contacts. It was already the vetted runner-up in docs/updates/soum_case_nominations.md.
